slides.title: The big idea
slides.html:
A congruence proof follows a pattern: mark the givens on the figure, find the three parts you need, and name the test.

Example: Given M is the midpoint of AD and of BC. Prove triangle AMB is congruent to triangle DMC. AM = DM and BM = CM (definition of midpoint). Angle AMB = angle DMC (vertical angles are equal). So the triangles are congruent by SAS. Look for shared sides (reflexive property) and vertical angles; they are often the hidden third part.
